text:
Leap years exist because Earth's orbit around the Sun takes about 365.2422 days, not a whole 365. Adding an extra day (February 29) every four years keeps the calendar aligned with the seasons.

The rule is refined to correct for the small excess: years divisible by 100 are not leap years, unless they're also divisible by 400. So 1900 was divisible by 100 but not by 400, making it a common year. The year 2000 was divisible by 400, so it was a leap year.
